How a canonical URL works

A page declares its preferred representative: A page with parameters or another duplicate entry can use rel=canonical in its head to point to the URL it prefers search systems to recognize as representative.

The visited URL and representative can differ: People may still open the parameterized current URL, and the address bar normally does not change because of canonical. The sitemap should use the chosen representative too.

What it is not

A canonical is a hint about which URL should represent a group to search systems. A redirect sends a visit from an old URL to a new one. Canonical usually does not change the address bar and is not a forced command; use a redirect when people must leave the old URL.
